task: This tiny shopping calculator gives wrong totals. First run its existing unit tests to see what is wrong, then fix calculator.py and rerun the tests. Keep the existing tests unchanged. Explain the failure and what you fixed.
model: real Q4 through COW HTTP on llm-60
operator_guidance: only initial natural-language task; no intervention
scope: fresh installed dev54 CLI autonomous repair, real Q4 COW HTTP, unchanged existing unit tests

outcome.answer: The existing tests initially failed with exit status 1: `test_one` expected `total([7]) == 7` but got `0`, and `test_many` expected `total([2, 3, 4]) == 9` but got `5`. The cause was in `calculator.py`: `total` returned `sum(prices[:-1])`, which deliberately drops the last price. For `[7]`, that leaves an empty list, summing to `0`; for `[2, 3, 4]`, it sums only `2 + 3`, giving `5`. I changed the return expression to `sum(prices)` so every item is included. I did not modify `test_calculator.py`. The rerun named check `calculator_unit_tests` ran `python3 -m unittest test_calculator -v`, exited 0, and reported all 3 tests OK.
